server.name: ci-mcp-server
server.description: MCP server for SAP CPI OData APIs

entitySets.description: SAP CPI integration packages (logical containers that group iFlows, value mappings, and other design-time artifacts)
integration flow (iFlow) design-time definitions — the editable integration logic before deployment

navigationProperties.name: Resources
navigationProperties.description: the bundled files (BPMN XML, scripts, schemas, WSDL) inside an iFlow artifact

navigationProperties.name: Configurations
navigationProperties.description: externalized configuration parameters (endpoint URLs, credentials aliases, custom properties) of an iFlow

entitySets.description: deployed (runtime) integration artifacts — check deployment status, version, and errors for running iFlows
value mapping design-time artifacts — lookup tables that translate codes/identifiers between sender and receiver systems

navigationProperties.name: ValMapSchema
navigationProperties.description: the source-to-target mapping schema rows that define how values are translated

entitySets.description: message mapping design-time artifacts — graphical structure-to-structure transformations between source and target message formats
script collection design-time artifacts — reusable Groovy or JavaScript libraries shared across multiple iFlows
message type design-time artifacts — XSD-based message type definitions used in service interfaces
fault message type design-time artifacts — XSD-based fault/error message type definitions used in service interfaces
data type design-time artifacts — XSD-based data type definitions used in message types and service interfaces
service interface design-time artifacts — WSDL-based service interface definitions describing operations and message structures
runtime service endpoints — URLs exposed by deployed iFlows, including protocol, entry points and API definitions
custom tag configurations — tenant-level labels used to categorize and filter integration packages
build and deploy task status — track whether an iFlow deployment is queued, running, or finished
message processing logs — execution history for integration flows, used to debug failed messages or monitor processing status

navigationProperties.name: Attachments
navigationProperties.description: attachments of the message processing log

navigationProperties.name: ErrorInformation
navigationProperties.description: error information for the message processing log

navigationProperties.name: AdapterAttributes
navigationProperties.description: adapter-specific metadata recorded during message processing

navigationProperties.name: CustomHeaderProperties
navigationProperties.description: custom header properties recorded during message processing

navigationProperties.name: MessageStoreEntries
navigationProperties.description: message store entries linked to this processing log

navigationProperties.name: Runs
navigationProperties.description: processing runs and run steps for this message processing log

entitySets.description: ID mapping entries — used for exactly-once processing to map source IDs to target IDs and prevent duplicate messages
idempotent repository entries — duplicate-check records that ensure a message is processed only once
data store entries — key-value records persisted by iFlows for cross-message data sharing or temporary storage
integration flow variables — runtime variables persisted between iFlow executions (e.g. timestamps, counters, delta tokens)
number range configurations — auto-incrementing counters used to generate unique sequence numbers in iFlows
message store entries — full messages explicitly persisted via the Persist step for later retrieval or retry
JMS broker instances — the messaging broker(s) provisioned on the tenant, including capacity and queue counts
JMS queue resources — individual message queues with their current depth, capacity, and consumer status
system log files — tenant-level runtime logs (HTTP, default trace, audit) for low-level troubleshooting
archived log files — compressed historical log bundles available for download
keystore entries in the tenant certificate store — SSL/TLS certificates, key pairs, and trusted CA certificates used for secure connections
certificate chain resources — the full X.509 certificate chains associated with keystore entries, useful for verifying trust paths
SSH key resources — public/private key pairs used for SFTP adapter connectivity
user credential artifacts — stored username/password pairs deployed as security material for basic-auth connections
OAuth2 client credential artifacts — client ID/secret pairs and token endpoints for OAuth2 client-credentials-grant connections
secure parameter artifacts — encrypted key-value entries referenced in iFlow externalized parameters to store sensitive configuration values
certificate-to-user mappings — rules that map inbound client certificates to CPI user roles for certificate-based authentication
access policies — fine-grained authorization rules that restrict which user roles can access specific integration artifacts

navigationProperties.name: ArtifactReferences
navigationProperties.description: the specific integration artifacts (iFlows, packages) governed by this access policy

entitySets.description: partner directory entries — trading partners (e.g. customers, suppliers) whose connection details and parameters drive dynamic iFlow routing
partner-specific string parameters — text configuration values (e.g. endpoint URLs, format codes) keyed by partner ID and parameter ID
partner-specific binary parameters — file-based configuration (e.g. XSLT stylesheets, certificates, mapping files) keyed by partner ID and parameter ID
alternative partner entries — additional identifiers (agency/scheme pairs like DUNS, GLN) that map to a primary partner ID for flexible partner lookup
authorized user entries — users permitted to send messages on behalf of a specific partner, used for sender-side authorization checks

API usage and performance metrics in UTC — pre-aggregated data including call counts, response times (sum/avg/min/max), request sizes, errors, target response times, and processing latencies, grouped by time dimensions (year, month, day, hour, minute) and dimensions like API proxy, application, product, developer, response code, and request method

SAP API Management API providers - named backend connections (URL or BTP destination, host, port, SSL, auth type, on-premise flag) that API proxies target. Creating a proxy starts here: create or pick a provider (POST with name, title, destType, host/url, port, useSSL), then point the proxy's target endpoint at it via provider_id; alternatively a target endpoint can use a plain url with provider_id 'NONE'

SAP API Management API proxies - the managed facade in front of a backend, with proxy endpoints (base_path, virtual hosts, route rules), target endpoints (backend url or API provider), policies, and lifecycle state (state is DEPLOYED once deployed). Key is name, e.g. path "('MyAPI')" or "(name='MyAPI')". Create-proxy flow: (1) API provider via APIProviders, or skip and use a plain target url; (2) POST the proxy here with name, title, releaseStatus 'Active', service_code 'REST' and deep-inserted proxyEndPoints (name 'default', base_path, isDefault true, virtualhosts linked to a VirtualHosts entry by __metadata uri, routeRules) and targetEndPoints (name 'default', isDefault true, url or provider_id plus relativePath); (3) deploy it via APIProxyDeployments_create and confirm with APIProxyDeployments_get; (4) only then attach it to a product via APIProducts - a proxy must be deployed before it can be added to a product. Use $expand=proxyEndPoints/routeRules,proxyEndPoints/virtualhosts,targetEndPoints to see a working proxy's full shape before creating a similar one

SAP API Management API proxy deployments - one record per deployed API proxy, keyed by the proxy name, with revisionID and state (DEPLOYED or UNDEPLOYED). Deploying a proxy is a create on this entity set, not an action: POST with body {"name": "<proxy name>", "state": "DEPLOYED"} (the same POST with state UNDEPLOYED undeploys it). A proxy must be deployed before it can be attached to an API product

SAP API Management API products - bundles of deployed API proxies published to developers, with quota (quotaCount, quotaInterval, quotaTimeUnit), scope, and isRestricted flag. A product links proxies through its many-to-many apiProxies navigation property: in the create or update body pass "apiProxies": [{"__metadata": {"uri": "APIProxies('<proxy name>')"}}]. Only deployed proxies can be attached (check APIProxyDeployments first). Updates are a full-replacement PUT to APIProducts('<product>'), so send the full entity including every apiProxies link you want to keep. PUT needs the cloud-practitioner/odata-mcp-proxy fork build; the published odata-mcp-proxy 1.x sends PATCH, which API Management may reject for link changes

SAP API Management proxy endpoints - the client-facing side of an API proxy (base_path, isDefault, linked virtual hosts, route rules to target endpoints, pre/post flows), keyed by a generated id and linked to their proxy via FK_API_NAME. Usually created by deep insert with the proxy; filter by FK_API_NAME to find a proxy's endpoints

SAP API Management target endpoints - the backend side of an API proxy (a plain url, or provider_id naming an API provider plus relativePath, with load balancer settings and pre/post flows), keyed by a generated id and linked to their proxy via FK_API_NAME. Usually created by deep insert with the proxy; filter by FK_API_NAME to find a proxy's targets

SAP API Management virtual hosts - the hostnames and ports (virtual_host, virtual_port, isSSL, isDefault) on which proxy endpoints are exposed. Look up the default virtual host's id here and link it from a new proxy endpoint's virtualhosts

SAP API Management environment key value maps - named, optionally encrypted maps that policies read at runtime (e.g. backend credentials or settings), keyed by name. Create a map with its entries in one call by deep-inserting keyMapEntryValues ([{"name": "<key>", "value": "<value>"}])
SAP API Management key value map entries - single key/value pairs inside an environment key value map, keyed by map_name (the owning map) and name (the entry key)

SAP API Management scoped (generic) key value maps - key value maps bound to a scope and scopeId (the level and owning artifact the map belongs to), optionally encrypted, keyed by name, scope and scopeId. Create a map with its entries in one call by deep-inserting genericKeyMapEntryValues
SAP API Management scoped key value map entries - single key/value pairs inside a scoped key value map, keyed by mapName, name (the entry key), scope and scopeId

SAP API Management API resources - the documented operations of an API proxy (resource_path, title, description, and which HTTP methods are enabled via isGetChecked, isPostChecked and the like), keyed by a generated id and linked to their proxy endpoint via FK_PROXYENDPOINT_ID. Usually created by deep insert with the proxy endpoint; filter by FK_PROXYENDPOINT_ID (an APIProxyEndPoints id) to list one proxy's resources, and $expand=documentations to read their documentation

SAP API Management API resource documentation - the per-locale documentation text (content, mime_type) of an API resource, keyed by id and locale and linked to the resource via FK_APIRESOURCE_ID. Filter by FK_APIRESOURCE_ID to read one resource's documentation

SAP API Management proxy policies - the policy definitions attached to an API proxy (name, type, policy_content holding the policy XML), keyed by a generated id and linked to their proxy via FK_API_NAME. Filter by FK_API_NAME to list one proxy's policies. A policy only runs once a step in a proxy or target endpoint flow references it by name, and proxy changes take effect after the proxy is redeployed via APIProxyDeployments

SAP API Management API proxy revisions - the GetAllRevisions function import, which returns every saved revision of one API proxy (revisionID, revisionName, revisionDescription, change history). Pass the proxy name as a query parameter in path, e.g. "?apiProxyName='MyAPI'"; there is no key lookup

SAP API Management product custom attributes - name/value pairs attached to an API product (at most 18 per product; name up to 255 and value up to 1024 characters) that the Verify API Key, Access Token and Access Entity policies can read at runtime, keyed by entityId (the product name) and name. Filter by entityId to list one product's attributes; they can also be deep-inserted as additionalProperties when creating a product

SAP API Management rate plans - monetization plans (name, currency, frequency, type Basic or Tier, isActive, isPublished, validFrom/validTo, and rate as a JSON string such as {"baseRate":20,"tiers":[{"fromCount":0,"toCount":0,"ratePerCall":1}]}) that are attached to API products to bill application developers, keyed by a generated id. Filter with isActive eq true for active plans. Updates are a full-replacement PUT to RatePlans('<id>'), so send the whole plan. PUT needs the cloud-practitioner/odata-mcp-proxy fork build; the published odata-mcp-proxy 1.x sends PATCH

SAP API Management applications - developer applications subscribed to API products (title, status_code, callbackurl, the developer via FK_DEVELOPER_ID, and the application key and secret that callers present to the Verify API Key and OAuth policies), keyed by a generated id. Read-only here. The response includes app_key and app_secret, so use $select to leave them out unless the user asks for the credentials; $expand=apiProducts lists the subscribed products and $expand=developer the owner

SAP API Management developers - the application developers registered for the API portal (firstName, lastName, emailId, country), keyed by a generated id. Read-only here; $expand=applications lists a developer's applications

SAP API Management certificate stores - named keystores and truststores (storeType KEYSTORE or TRUSTSTORE) that virtual hosts and target endpoints use for TLS, keyed by name. $expand=certificates lists a store's certificates. Create a store with its first certificate in one call by deep-inserting certificates (name, content as base64, and password for a keystore key pair)

SAP API Management certificates - the certificates inside a keystore or truststore (certName, format, validity via validFrom, expiryDate and isValid, issuer and subject details), keyed by name and storeName. Read-only here; filter by storeName to list one store's certificates, or by expiryDate to find certificates that are about to expire

SAP API Management certificate store references - named aliases (name, certificateStoreName, storeType) that point at a keystore or truststore, so virtual hosts and TLS settings can use the reference and a certificate rotation only repoints the reference, keyed by name. Create with {"name": "<reference>", "certificateStoreName": "<store>"}; updates are a PUT to CertificateStoreReferences('<reference>') with {"certificateStoreName": "<new store>"}. PUT needs the cloud-practitioner/odata-mcp-proxy fork build; the published odata-mcp-proxy 1.x sends PATCH

SAP API Management cache resources - named caches (at most 10) that the Populate, Lookup, Invalidate and Response Cache policies use instead of the shared cache when they name the cache in their CacheResource element, with in-memory and disk sizing, compression and expiry settings, keyed by name. Updates are a full-replacement PUT to CacheResources('<name>'), so send the whole cache definition. PUT needs the cloud-practitioner/odata-mcp-proxy fork build; the published odata-mcp-proxy 1.x sends PATCH

SAP API Management product access rules - access control rules that let only users with a given role discover or subscribe to a restricted API product (isRestricted true) in the Developer Hub. Each rule has ruleId (generated), entityId (the product name), actor ({"name": "<role name>", "type": "Role"}) and action (Discovery or Subscription), and only one rule may exist per product and action. Create with {"ruleId": "0000", "entityId": "<product>", "actor": {"name": "<role>", "type": "Role"}, "action": "Discovery"}; filter by entityId to list one product's rules

SAP API Management API proxy export - downloads one API proxy with its endpoints, resources and policies as a zip bundle (returned base64-encoded by the cloud-practitioner/odata-mcp-proxy fork build; the published odata-mcp-proxy 1.x corrupts the zip) for backup or for moving it to another API portal. Pass the proxy name as a query parameter in path, e.g. "?name=MyAPI". Export only: importing the zip back needs a multipart upload, which this server does not support
